findings.title: Complete-pooling LinearTrend regularization potential has inverted sign and wrong functional form
findings.expected: Notebook 09 spec: penalty = -phi*(w_target - w_source)^2, i.e. log-posterior must DECREASE when the slope deviates from the transferred source value; with loss_factor_for_tune=1 and source mean 0, potential(slope=1)-potential(slope=0) must be about -1.
findings.observed: probe output: 'pool=complete potential(slope=1)-potential(slope=0) = 1.000'. The code adds +loss_factor*abs(slope - slope_mean) (plus, not minus, and abs instead of square).
findings.consequence: With the paper-recommended loss_factor_for_tune=1, complete-pooling transfer actively rewards slope drift away from the source model, inverting the documented/paper regularization (the non-hierarchical transfer-learning result). Default 0 leaves it latent; the smart_home case study sweeps loss_factor={0,1}.
evidence: cmd output line: pool=complete   potential(slope=1)-potential(slope=0) =  1.000  (name: lt_0 - slope - loss)

findings.title: Individual-pooling LinearTrend regularization potential has inverted sign
findings.expected: Notebook 09 spec penalty = -phi*(w_target - w_source)^2; for 2 groups at slope=1, source mean 0, phi=1 the potential increase must be about -2.
findings.observed: probe output: 'pool=individual potential(slope=1)-potential(slope=0) = 2.112'. Code adds +loss_factor*sum(sqr(slope - slope_mu)) (sign inverted relative to the partial branch).
findings.consequence: Individual-pooling transfer with loss_factor_for_tune>0 pushes slopes away from the source instead of shrinking them; the same hyperparameter has the opposite effect depending on pool_type.
evidence: cmd output line: pool=individual potential(slope=1)-potential(slope=0) =  2.112  (name: lt_0 - slope - loss)

findings.title: loss_factor_for_tune has opposite sign in complete/individual vs partial LinearTrend pooling
findings.expected: The same hyperparameter should shrink the slope toward the transferred source value in every pooling mode: notebook 09 spec penalty = -phi*(w_target - w_source)^2 (negative phi flips to encourage deviation). All three modes should therefore show a negative potential increment at phi=1.
findings.observed: Potential increment at slope=1, source mean 0, phi=1 differs in sign/scale by pooling mode: complete +1.000, partial -2.112, individual +2.112. Only the partial branch uses the spec's negative squared penalty.
findings.consequence: Documented semantics of loss_factor_for_tune (positive = stronger constraint, negative = encourage deviation, notebook 09 §2) hold only for partial pooling; complete/individual invert the effect, and complete also changes the functional form (abs instead of squared). Ablations that sweep loss_factor across pooling modes compare non-comparable objectives.
evidence: cmd output: pool=complete potential(slope=1)-potential(slope=0) =  1.000; pool=partial ... = -2.112; pool=individual ... =  2.112

findings.title: Fourier individual-pooling prior_from_idata doubles prior variance and halves correlations
findings.expected: Notebook 08: prior_from_idata fits MultivariateNormal(mu, Sigma) to the source posterior and 'preserv[es] the covariance structure between all parameters'; target marginal sd and correlations should match the source (complete pooling does: var_ratio 1.001, corr 0.9013).
findings.observed: Individual branch builds beta = pm.Normal(mu=priors[prior_beta], sigma=beta_sd, shape=(n_groups, 2*order)), adding an independent N(0, diag(beta_sd^2)) on top of the MVN draw. Source sd [2.0065 2.0034 1.497 1.4915], corr[0,1] 0.9005; target sd [2.8397 2.8417 2.1241 2.105], var_ratio ~2.0, corr[0,1] 0.4515 (halved).
findings.consequence: Individual-pooling seasonal transfer is over-dispersed (2x variance) and the advertised covariance preservation of prior_from_idata is not delivered in this mode; same defect pattern in NormalConstant, UniformConstant and FlatTrend individual branches.
evidence: cmd output: pool=individual target sd=[2.8397 2.8417 2.1241 2.105 ] var_ratio=[2.003 2.012 2.013 1.992]; target corr[0,1]=0.4515 vs source corr[0,1]=0.9005
cmd output: pool=complete target sd=[2.0074 1.9973 1.5015 1.4855] var_ratio=[1.001 0.994 1.006 0.992]; target corr[0,1]=0.9013

findings.title: LinearTrend individual-pooling prior_from_idata doubles the slope prior variance
findings.expected: The transferred slope prior should have the source posterior variance (4.02) as in complete pooling, preserving the MVN marginal; a Normal prior needs a deterministic location, not a random MVN draw plus extra independent scale.
findings.observed: slope = pm.Normal(slope_key, mu=priors[prior_slope], sigma=slope_sd, shape=n_groups) with slope_sd from the source posterior; measured target variance 8.139 vs source 4.020 (ratio 2.024).
findings.consequence: Individual-pooling trend transfer is over-dispersed (2x prior variance) and all groups share the same random prior location draw, contradicting both the covariance-preservation claim and the independence implied by individual pooling.
evidence: cmd output: LinearTrend individual: source var=4.020 target var=8.139 ratio=2.024

findings.title: Parametric transfer uses the posterior mean, not the mode/MAP estimator the paper reports as better
findings.expected: Notebook 09 cell 4: 'The paper showed that centering priors around the mode rather than the mean can improve results, particularly for the trend slope'; a mode/MAP-centred transfer estimator would return a location at the posterior mode rather than the sample mean. (README documents mean as the default and mode as a manual override.)
findings.observed: On a strongly skewed Exp(1) posterior the helper returns loc=0.99851 exactly equal to the sample mean, while the histogram/KDE mode is 0.06202 (loc - mode = +0.936). No case-study script sets override_*_for_tune (grep: 1 hit, an sbatch README).
findings.consequence: The released default estimator is the posterior mean; the mode improvement the notebook attributes to the paper is not the default and is not exercised by any case-study artifact (no override_* use), so paper claims about mode-centred priors are not traceable to the snapshot's code or experiments.
evidence: cmd output: returned loc=0.99851  sample mean=0.99851  returned sd=1.00245  histogram-mode=0.06202; loc-mode = +0.93649
grep -rn override <snapshot>/case_studies | wc -l -> 1 (only case_studies/README.md:173 sbatch flags, no model overrides)

findings.title: Parametric transfer from a one-draw MAP posterior yields sigma=0 and breaks the Normal prior
findings.location: snapshot src/vangja/components/linear_trend.py:219 and src/vangja/components/fourier_seasonality.py:201 (posterior .std() used as prior sigma)
findings.expected: Notebook 08 comparison table: parametric transfer 'Works with MAP, ADVI, NUTS'; a Normal prior requires sigma>0, and a MAP posterior carries a single draw so a valid scale must be sourced elsewhere.
findings.observed: With a one-draw idata the helper returns (loc, sd) = (0.5, 0.0); evaluating pm.logp(pm.Normal.dist(0.5, 0.0), 0.5) raises ParameterValueError: sigma > 0.
findings.consequence: The documented 'Works with MAP' parametric transfer path is unusable: a MAP point estimate has one posterior draw, so the derived Normal prior has zero scale and the target model has no valid log-density (and fit(method=map/mapx) leaves self.trace=None, so there is not even an InferenceData to pass).
evidence: cmd output: returned (loc, sd) = (0.5, 0.0); Normal(loc, sd) logp at loc = ParameterValueError: sigma > 0

findings.title: Partial-pooling LinearTrend with n_changepoints=0 raises KeyError on the missing delta posterior
findings.location: snapshot src/vangja/components/linear_trend.py:504-524 (_partial_definition delta handling not guarded by n_changepoints)
findings.expected: With n_changepoints=0 there is no delta parameter, so transfer must not query the delta posterior; the individual-pooling branch demonstrates the intended guard (linear_trend.py: 'if self.n_changepoints:').
findings.observed: _partial_definition calls _get_delta_params_from_idata whenever delta_pool_type=='partial' (default), even with n_changepoints=0; probe raises KeyError 'Could not find node at lt_0 - delta', while the identical individual-pooling setup returns OK.
findings.consequence: A valid model configuration (LinearTrend with no changepoints, partial pooling, transfer) crashes before inference with a KeyError; the individual branch guards the same code path with 'if self.n_changepoints', so the dispatch is inconsistent across pooling modes.
evidence: cmd output: partial -> KeyError 'Could not find node at lt_0 - delta'; individual OK
